atoms.text: La Tomatina Festival is a tomato food fight festival located in Buñol, Spain, not far from Valencia. It is the largest food fight in the world, and thousands of people travel from all around the world to participate. Before 2013, as many as 50,000 people attended the festival. Starting in 2013, there were rules limiting the amount of people who could visit the festival. Since 2013, 20,000 people attend every year.

The festival happens on the last Wednesday of August every year. A cannon marks the beginning of the festival. Once the festival begins, six trucks drive through the streets filled to the brim with tomatoes. The food fight only lasts for one hour, and then a clean-up crew clears the streets of all the tomatoes.

The festival started in 1945, but the origins of the festival are unclear. Some say that the festival was started by a group of children in the town square, while others say that a dispute between farmers caused the festival. Another story is that during a parade someone’s costume was broken, and the person became so enraged that they grabbed produce and began throwing it at people. The next year a group of young people returned on the same day and began the tradition of the food fight.
